records.issue_text: [BUG] The cache check is not re-evaluated after acquiring the write lock, so concurrent first requests each rebuild and overwrite the assets. Under concurrent cold-start requests in non-Dev, N simultaneous goroutines all see nil, all take the write lock in turn, and each re-runs the expensive build (dist scan / checksum work) instead of the intended single build; the last writer wins the cache, so callers receive different EntryPointAssets instances for the same key, defeating the cache exactly when load is highest.
records.rationale: The diff shows a read lock to fetch `ret := entryPointAssetsCache`, returns it if non-Dev and non-nil, then unconditionally takes the write lock when `ret` is nil. After acquiring the write lock, there is no second check of `entryPointAssetsCache` before proceeding to build (`entryPointAssetsCacheMu.Lock(); defer ...`). This allows multiple concurrent cold-start requests to each observe nil under RLock and then, one-by-one under the write lock, redundantly rebuild and overwrite the cache instead of a single build.

records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The PR adds concurrency control (sync.RWMutex) and a new TODO comment, which is a race-condition fix plus code hygiene, not the stated 'asset optimization' work — it is implementation not traceable to the PR's stated intent. Reviewers and future archaeologists tracing this diff cannot tell why the lock was introduced here (no data race issue is referenced); if a separate race-fix PR lands, the two changes will conflict and the duplicated effort surfaces as merge friction for whoever reconciles them.
